parameterExtensions.contract: Add movingMean and movingSum operations with a required non-negative row frame preceding value and optional following defaulting to zero.
Add angle to the closed removable channel vocabulary and rematerialize the point or Tick at its unrotated baseline.
Add stack: 'center' for non-negative grouped area series; each partition begins at negative half of its total.
Add layout: 'center' for categorical area color and wrap encodeY({ stack: 'center' }).

typeContracts.name: TimeUnit
typeContracts.policy: Output is a finite UTC bucket-start timestamp; week and configurable timezone are excluded.

typeContracts.name: CategoryOrder
typeContracts.shape: { values: readonly CategoryValue[] } | { by: 'category' | 'count' | { field: FieldName; aggregate: 'sum' | 'mean' | 'min' | 'max' }; direction?: 'ascending' | 'descending' }
typeContracts.policy: Explicit lists append omitted observed values in first-appearance order; computed ties use stable first appearance.

typeContracts.name: MovingWindowOperation
typeContracts.shape: { op: 'movingMean' | 'movingSum'; field: FieldName; as: FieldName; frame: { preceding: NonNegativeInteger; following?: NonNegativeInteger } }
typeContracts.policy: Frames count sorted rows inside one partition and truncate at partition edges.

gateDecisions.reason: It matches current temporal normalization and keeps derived values directly usable by the existing time scale.
Ordering changes chart meaning and must replay across scale, guide, facet and Canvas rematerialization.
It is deterministic with the existing partition/sort contract and avoids implicit time-interval semantics.
It gives Tick one unambiguous geometry contract without inventing plot-edge rug placement.
Directional data remains literal: 0 is up, positive is clockwise, and values are not silently normalized from their data domain.
These item glyphs have a clear rotation center; line, area, bar, rule, rect, text and arc require different semantics.
It produces the useful centered stream layout while avoiding signed and wiggle algorithms with different meaning.
